hints.title: Core Idea
hints.text: Find employees whose project workload strictly exceeds the average workload of their respective team.

hints.title: Key Observation
hints.text: Join the Project table with the Employees table and compute the average workload partitioned by team.

hints.title: Query Structure
hints.text: Use a window function or CTE to calculate team average workload, then filter where workload is greater than the team average and sort by employee id and project id.

hints.title: Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
WITH T AS (
    SELECT
        p.employee_id,
        p.project_id,
        e.name AS employee_name,
        p.workload AS project_workload,
        AVG(p.workload) OVER (PARTITION BY e.team) AS avg_workload
    FROM Project AS p
    JOIN Employees AS e ON p.employee_id = e.employee_id
)
SELECT
    employee_id,
    project_id,
    employee_name,
    project_workload
FROM T
WHERE project_workload > avg_workload
ORDER BY employee_id, project_id;
```

complexity.notes: Equi-join followed by windowed partition average.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Correlated subqueries per row lead to quadratic execution time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Compute team average using window functions partitioned by team.

WITH T AS (
    SELECT
        p.employee_id,
        p.project_id,
        e.name AS employee_name,
        p.workload AS project_workload,
        AVG(p.workload) OVER (PARTITION BY e.team) AS avg_workload
    FROM Project AS p
    JOIN Employees AS e ON p.employee_id = e.employee_id
)
SELECT
    employee_id,
    project_id,
    employee_name,
    project_workload
FROM T
WHERE project_workload > avg_workload
ORDER BY employee_id, project_id;

import pandas as pd

def employees_with_above_avg_workload(project: pd.DataFrame, employees: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = project.merge(employees, on='employee_id')
    df['avg_workload'] = df.groupby('team')['workload'].transform('mean')
    ans = df[df['workload'] > df['avg_workload']][['employee_id', 'project_id', 'name', 'workload']]
    ans = ans.rename(columns={'name': 'employee_name', 'workload': 'project_workload'})
    return ans.sort_values(by=['employee_id', 'project_id'])
